actor: Non-GPU inference-silicon vendor commercial / field-engineering lead
job: Convert in-volume Corsair shipments and design-win pilots into a named, on-record at-scale production deployment with a hyperscaler or neocloud.
outcome: A signed multi-rack purchase or on-record customer announcement naming the operator and workload running Corsair-class silicon in production at scale.
motivation: Volume ship to unnamed priority customers is not yet franchise proof; a named at-scale win establishes the category against GPU economics.

task.where: Priority-customer inference deployments fronting Blackwell hosts

actor: Rack-scale inference reference-design integration partner (networking / switch-silicon / server OEM)
job: Harden the SquadRack-class reference design so Corsair cards ship as a production-ready inference rack rather than a bare accelerator.
outcome: A deployable multi-rack inference system an operator can stand up at scale, removing integration risk that blocks pilot-to-production conversion.
motivation: At-scale buyers commit only to production-ready racks; packaging-only deals do not convert, so integration maturity gates the named win.

task.who: Networking, switch-silicon, and server-OEM rack-integration engineers
task.what: Productize a rack-scale Corsair inference reference design
task.where: SquadRack-class reference rack co-built across vendors
task.why: Operators deploy production-ready racks, not bare accelerators

actor: Hyperscaler / neocloud / large-enterprise inference-infrastructure procurement and platform team
job: Evaluate Corsair-class in-memory-compute silicon against GPU baselines and move a qualifying workload from evaluation into at-scale production.
outcome: A public on-record commitment naming the operator and workload, or a disclosed capacity/revenue milestone, deploying the silicon in production at scale.
motivation: GPU-only inference economics leave a memory-bandwidth-bound cost and energy gap that Corsair-class latency and efficiency gains can close.
